slots.body:

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 26, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,677.33, up 53.65 points (+0.7%), with an intraday range of 7,639.70 to 7,702.13.
The Nasdaq Composite outpaced the Dow, rising 0.8% to 26,169.38 vs the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 52,361.58 (+0.3%).
The Russell 2000 added 0.4% to 2,786.42.

The VIX fell 5.4% to 18.39 (prior close 19.45), the largest percentage move among the injected U.S. index set — a lower reading on a day when broad equities still advanced.

Two U.S. activity gauges printed on the calendar: the Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September at 0.07 (estimate −0.10; prior −0.08), and the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index for October at 13.4 (estimate 7.0; prior 9.8).
Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-10-23) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.31 percentage points.

Nasdaq sector averages favored Real Estate (+1.3%), Consumer Cyclical (+1.1%), and Technology (+1.0%).
Communication Services lagged at about −1.2%; Basic Materials was slightly negative.
That split fits a day when large tech and semis were firmer while some megcap communication names sold off.

Chip and AI-adjacent megacaps in the injected close included:
- $MSFT +1.5% to 532.60
- $AMD +2.8% to 531.28
- $AVGO +2.3% to 329.17
- $TSM +1.4% to 424.37
- $ASML +1.2% to 1,590.90

$META bucked that group at −1.9% to 630.56 amid post-close coverage on AI financing needs.
$GOOGL / $GOOG were down about −1.1% / −1.0%.

Brazil risk dominated the extreme movers: $EWZ −19.8%, $XP −48.4%, $BBD −28.0%, and $ITUB −20.4% among actives, while U.S. mega energy was mixed — $XOM +0.7% to 184.54 (session high equal to 52-week high in the quote) and $CVX −0.5% to 232.01.

$VZ −3.5% followed results with EPS $1.31 vs $1.27 estimated and revenue about $34.31B vs $34.77B expected.
$CDNS +1.8% after EPS $2.11 vs $2.05 est and revenue beat; $RMBS +5.5% on EPS $0.84 vs $0.789 est.
$AMKR −6.3% with revenue about $1.99B vs $2.04B expected.
$PSA reported EPS $1.69 vs $2.49 est; the stock closed −0.9% to 306.97.
$WELL rose 1.4% with revenue above the estimate though EPS $0.54 trailed the $0.64 consensus in the calendar.

Oil-linked quotes softened: Brent crude futures −1.0% to 114.64; the injected USO proxy −1.9% to 166.23.
Gold futures −0.3% to 4,026.60.
The dollar proxy UUP +0.2% to 29.01; EUR/USD roughly flat at 1.12 (−0.1%).
Bitcoin −0.2% to 79,814.03.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included Nikkei 225 +1.9% to 63,381.29, FTSE 100 +0.7%, and Hang Seng −0.2%.
Headlines in the feed pointed to chip strength in Japan and oil easing on Middle East diplomacy talk, with attention on the upcoming Fed decision — descriptive context only, not a forecast for U.S. rates.
